newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir shops shut in human rights protest.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir shops shut in human rights protest.

text.p: A strike called by separatists in protest against alleged human rights abuses by Indian security forces closed down shops and businesses on Saturday in Srinagar, Kashmir's biggest city.

"We appeal to Kashmiris to observe a complete strike on Saturday to show solidarity with the women of Kashmir who are the latest targets of police and other counter-insurgency forces," said Mohammad Yasin Malik, spokesman for the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, Kashmir's leading separatist alliance.
The Hurriyat called the strike after a 45-year-old woman died of a heart attack when her house was raided by police on Wednesday.
The Hurriyat alleged that another woman was severely tortured by police. A police spokesman denied the charge.
Police on Thursday fired shots into the air and used teargas to disperse hundreds of demonstrators protesting at alleged undue use of force by Indian troops during the raid.
"Hundreds of Kashmir women have been raped, molested and tortured by security forces," Malik said.
Indian authorities deny the separatists' allegations of excesses by security forces on women. They say they investigate all such charges and punish those found guilty.

Officials say at least 224 army and paramilitary soldiers have been punished for human rights violations since a separatist rebellion erupted in 1990 in Kashmir, where dozens of guerrilla groups are fighting for merger with neighbouring Pakistan or independence.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed over the past seven years.
